tagline: Gettysburg to Monticello on the old Rogues' Road.
intro: From Gettysburg the byway runs south on US 15 under Catoctin Mountain to Frederick, crosses the Potomac at Point of Rocks, and goes on through Leesburg, Warrenton, Culpeper and Orange. Then Virginia side roads carry it on to Monticello, 180 miles in all.

Much of it follows the old Carolina Road, one of the busiest roads in 18th-century America. Drovers took swine, cattle, sheep and even turkeys down it, and since some picked up local cows on the way, Fauquier farmers called it the Rogues' Road.

moments.title: Catoctin Furnace
moments.text: Enslaved and free ironworkers here made shells for Yorktown. The furnace, built in 1774, ran until 1903, and in 1923 the workers' families were allowed to buy their houses.

moments.title: Point of Rocks
moments.text: In 1828 the canal and the railroad went to court over the narrow gap between the Potomac and Catoctin Mountain. Six years later they agreed to share it.

moments.title: Gordonsville
moments.text: Washington, Jefferson and Lafayette all stopped at Nathaniel Gordon's tavern. The town now bills itself as the Fried Chicken Capital of the World.
